J-REINS Act of 2025

An Act to Rein in Excessive Judicial Overreach and Preserve Executive Authority

Section 1. Short Title

This Act may be cited as the "Judicial Restraint on Excessive Injunctions Needing Scrutiny" or “J-REINS Act.”

Section 2. Purpose

The purpose of this Act is to prevent inferior federal courts from issuing nationwide injunctions that usurp or impinge upon the plenary powers of the Executive Branch, ensuring that judicial authority remains within its constitutional bounds and subject to democratic accountability.

Section 3. Limitation on Nationwide Injunctions

(a) Prohibition: No district court or circuit court of appeals may issue an injunction or equitable relief that:

(1) Applies beyond the parties and geographic jurisdiction of the issuing court; or

(2) Directly mandates or prohibits actions by the President or Executive Branch agencies in the exercise of their constitutional or statutory authority, unless expressly authorized by Congress.

(b) Scope: 
This limitation applies to all cases, including but not limited to immigration enforcement, personnel decisions, and regulatory funding allocations.

(1) Any injunction exceeding the scope of this Act shall not impede the expenditure of funds appropriated by Congress for Executive Branch operations unless explicitly authorized in the appropriation.

Section 4. Congressional Review and Approval

(a) Submission: 
If a federal court seeks to issue an injunction with nationwide effect or that impacts Executive plenary powers, the court must submit its proposed order to Congress within 120 hours, along with a statement justifying its necessity and constitutional basis. Failure to do so renders the injunction invalid.

(b) Approval: 
Such an injunction shall not take effect unless approved by a joint resolution of Congress within 45 days of submission. Absent congressional approval within 45 days, the injunction is null and void. Pending such approval, the injunction shall apply only to the named parties in the case, and the judicial district that so ruled.

Section 5. Supreme Court Exception

This Act does not restrict the Supreme Court’s authority to issue nationwide relief, provided such relief adheres to constitutional limits on judicial power.

Section 6. Severability

If any provision of this Act is held invalid, the remainder shall not be affected and shall continue in full force and effect.

Section 7. Effective Date

This Act shall take effect 30 days after its enactment.
